title: The polynomial specialization conjecture for solid-partition weights
statement:
Let $\pi$ be a solid partition, let $\pi_{111}$ denote its height, and let $\mathsf{w}_\pi$ be defined using the unique signs in the affine DT4 vertex conjecture. Let $L_\pi(d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)$ be the corresponding tautological Euler-class contribution.

**Polynomial specialization conjecture.** The following properties hold: (a) $L_\pi(0,0,0,-d)\mathsf{w}_\pi$ has no pole at $\lambda_4=-(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3)$; (b) its specialization at $\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0$ is independent of $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$; and (c) there exists a rational number $\omega_\pi\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$, independent of $d$, such that

$$
L_\pi(0,0,0,-d)\mathsf{w}_\pi\big|_{\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0}=(-1)^{|\pi|}\omega_\pi\prod_{l=1}^{\pi_{111}}(d-(l-1)).
$$

In particular, for $d\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, the left-hand side vanishes when $\pi_{111}>d$ and otherwise has the same sign as $(-1)^\pi$. The paper gives finite-size and special-case evidence, but the general claim remains open.
source_name: Yalong Cao and Martijn Kool, “Zero-dimensional Donaldson-Thomas invariants of Calabi-Yau 4-folds”, arXiv:1712.07347 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).
